exposure: Uterine closure technique (Technique A: endometrium-free double-layer closure; Technique B: single- or double-layer routine endo-myometrial closure)
cohort: The study included 172 patients who had undergone at least one prior cesarean delivery, evaluated for niche via saline infusion sonohysterography (SIS).
finding: Technique B (single- or double-layer routine endo-myometrial closure) was associated with significantly increased adjusted odds of clinically significant niches (5.6 to 11-fold) compared to Technique A (endometrium-free double-layer closure) across repeat, lower-order, and higher-order cesarean subgroups.
cross-section timing: Post-cesarean, evaluated via saline infusion sonohysterography (SIS).
